## Accessibility Issue: Remove-document button has no accessible name

**Bug ID:** `A11Y-cb692d7d` (instance) / `A11Y-99471cd8` (pattern)
**URL:** https://apply.ruralgrants.example.gov/application/step-2
**XPath:** `//ul[contains(@class,'uploaded-docs')]/li[3]//button[contains(@class,'doc-remove')]`
**Full DOM path:** Not available. The scan's `target` selector for this node begins at `ul.uploaded-docs` and includes no ancestor markup above it (no `body`/`main`/`form` wrapper is reported). Populating a root-relative (`/html/body/...`) path would fabricate DOM structure not present in the scan output; obtain via live DOM inspection if a full ancestor chain is needed for dynamic-ID debugging.
**WCAG SC:** 4.1.2 — Name, Role, Value (Level A)
**Baseline test:** 5.A-ControlName *(declared Section 508 audit `rga-portal-2026q3`)*
**Rule:** axe-core 4.9.1 — `button-name`
**Severity:** Critical
**Frequency:** 1 instance on this page in this scan (1 node reported). No multi-page crawl data was included in the scan output, so site-wide occurrence cannot be determined — not inferred beyond what was reported. The failing control is a per-row "remove" button in a repeating uploaded-documents list (`li:nth-child(3)`), so this defect likely recurs on every row with an uploaded file; unconfirmed for rows 1–2 and any additional rows, pending a follow-up check.
**Screen type:** desktop | **Colour mode:** light *(default — not reported in scan output)*

### HTML Snippet

```html
<button class="doc-remove">
  <svg aria-hidden="true" viewBox="0 0 16 16">
    <path d="M4 4l8 8m0-8l-8 8"/>
  </svg>
</button>
```

### Description

The "remove" control for the third item in the uploaded-documents list (`ul.uploaded-docs`) is a `<button>` containing only a decorative `<svg>` icon marked `aria-hidden="true"`. It has no visible text, no `aria-label`, no `aria-labelledby`, and no `title` attribute, so it has no accessible name (axe-core rule `button-name`, help text: "Buttons must have discernible text"; helpUrl: https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.9/button-name).

Tags reported by axe-core: `cat.name-role-value`, `wcag2a`, `wcag412`, `ACT`, `TTv5`, `TT6.a`. The `TTv5`/`TT6.a` tags associate this rule with a DHS Trusted Tester v5 test case (exact sub-test scope not independently verified here). No specific ACT rule identifier was included in the scan output, so none is cited above.

This is not just a missing-label technicality: the page renders one visually identical icon-only "remove" button per uploaded document. Even after a label is added, a generic label such as `aria-label="Remove"` applied identically to every row would still leave every button announcing the same name — a screen reader user would still be unable to tell which document a given button removes without extra exploration. See Suggested Fix.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Navigate to https://apply.ruralgrants.example.gov/application/step-2 (the document-upload step of the application).
2. Ensure the "uploaded documents" list (`ul.uploaded-docs`) has at least 3 items, so a third `li` with a `button.doc-remove` control is present.
3. Tab to (or inspect via DevTools' Accessibility pane, or re-run an axe-core scan against) the "remove" button on the third list item.
4. Check the computed accessible name for that button.

*Detected via automated scan (axe-core 4.9.1, per scan metadata); the exact CLI/invocation command was not included in the provided scan output, so it is not reproduced here.*

### Expected Behaviour

The control exposes a distinguishing accessible name that identifies both the action and its target, e.g. "Remove [document filename], button" — sufficient for a user managing multiple uploaded documents to know which file a given control affects.

### Actual Behaviour

Per the accessible-name computation for this markup (no inner text, no `aria-label`, no `aria-labelledby`, no `title`, and the only child content is an `aria-hidden` SVG), the button exposes no accessible name; assistive technology would announce it only as "button." This is derived from the DOM structure and axe-core's failure summary, not from a live assistive-technology test performed as part of this scan.

### Testing Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Browser | Chrome 126 (126.0.0.0) |
| OS | macOS 14.5 (Intel) |
| Screen reader | N/A — automated scan only; no assistive technology used in this pass |
| Testing tool | axe-core 4.9.1 |
| Viewport | 1280 × 800 px |

### Impact

Blind and low-vision screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) cannot determine what this control does or which document it affects — every "remove" button in the uploaded-documents list would announce identically as an unnamed "button." Because the action is destructive (it removes an uploaded file from a government benefits application before submission), an applicant who cannot identify the correct control risks deleting the wrong required document, or may avoid the control entirely out of uncertainty. Voice-control users (Dragon NaturallySpeaking, Voice Control) cannot target the control by speaking a label, since none exists. Users with low vision relying on screen magnification may lose the surrounding row context at high zoom and have no programmatic confirmation of which row's button has focus.

### Suggested Fix (optional)

```html
<!-- Current (broken) -->
<button class="doc-remove">
  <svg aria-hidden="true" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M4 4l8 8m0-8l-8 8"/></svg>
</button>

<!-- Fixed: aria-label naming the action AND the specific document -->
<button class="doc-remove" aria-label="Remove {{ document.filename }}">
  <svg aria-hidden="true" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M4 4l8 8m0-8l-8 8"/></svg>
</button>
```

A generic `aria-label="Remove document"` applied identically to every row would silence the axe-core `button-name` rule but would not fix the underlying problem, since every button would still announce the same name. The label must incorporate data specific to that row — for example the filename already rendered as visible text elsewhere in the same `<li>` — either via a per-document dynamic `aria-label` (shown above) or via `aria-labelledby` pointing at an `id` on that existing filename text, which keeps the label in sync automatically.
